topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the learning outcomes and presenting the conceptual framework of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and proliferation signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase and Wnt/beta-catenin pathways enable cancer cells to sustain proliferative signaling and resist inhibitory cues.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how cancers in hematopoietic and intestinal tissues prevent precursor cells from exiting the cell cycle and completing terminal differentiation.

topics.label: Resistance to programmed cell death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells evade apoptosis by disrupting the balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic regulators downstream of p53.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress response mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells overcome cellular lifespan limits by reactivating telomerase to bypass senescence and how these pathways integrate with p53 stress surveillance.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the biochemical mechanisms, diagnostic utility, and epigenetic consequences of altered cellular metabolism and the Warburg effect in tumors.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how developing tumors overcome oxygen and nutrient diffusion limits by tipping the regulatory balance to stimulate new blood vessel growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and genetics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the multi-step metastatic cascade, clinical tracking using circulating tumor cells, and the genomic characteristics underlying secondary tumor colonization.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reflecting on the integration of cancer hallmarks and providing closing remarks.
